A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STAIR and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Retained material can be reliably matched across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results for LLaMA and Qwen, baseline comparisons, ablations, test-time scaling experiments, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds reward-function experiments, inference comparisons, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The structured-CoT training, SI-MCTS reward R=SH+2S, iterative step-level DPO, and PRM-guided inference remain unchanged. Appendix B.2.2 newly documents rating prompts and a refusal/length reward heuristic, without establishing that the underlying procedure was revised.

E1.justification: Training still uses PKU-SafeRLHF, JailbreakV-28k, and UltraFeedback, with the same ten evaluation benchmarks. The added analyses reuse existing datasets and tasks rather than introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 directly compares self-rewarded Best-of-4 inference against PRM-ranked Best-of-4 on STAIR-SFT and STAIR-DPO-1. The original training baselines and open-source/commercial comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new reward-function experiment uses 1,000 safety and 1,000 helpfulness prompts for one round of LLaMA step-level DPO. Additional evaluations compare rewarders under Best-of-4 and measure token counts and latency, including Best-of-4/8 costs. Previously reported main experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 adds reward-function sensitivity experiments, self-rewarding-versus-PRM inference controls, and training/inference cost analyses. These substantially broaden examination of the reward design, reward-model utility, and computational practicality beyond the retained data-balance, stepwise-training, and iteration ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. New statements about 'higher variance' and 'insignificant differences' provide no statistical estimates or testing procedures.

E6.justification: Original table values and plotted findings are retained, while new Tables 3–5 add substantial results on reward sensitivity, inference selection, and computational overhead. For DPO-1, self-rewarded/PRM Best-of-4 scores are 0.7370/0.7384 on StrongReject and 32.03%/33.11% on AlpacaEval. Table 5 newly reports DPO-3 StrongReject latency of 0.308 seconds, rising to 0.628/1.069 seconds with Best-of-4/8. These are added results, not established version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The reward assumptions, Theorem 2.1, and Appendix B.1 theorem, proof, and corollary are unchanged. Algorithm 1 merely reverses the order of equivalent reward terms; the new reward experiments instantiate the existing function family.

C1.justification: The claims about introspective reasoning improving safety while preserving helpfulness, iterative self-improvement, and Claude-3.5-comparable jailbreak resistance remain unchanged. The abstract newly foregrounds the theoretically grounded reward already presented in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that reward-form insensitivity supports the simple design and that PRM training averages noisy self-reward signals. It also discusses offline generation costs, practical inference overhead, and adjustable search budgets. These extend the supporting rationale without replacing the original interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2.2 adds exact helpfulness/safety rating prompts and discloses a reward heuristic using 'sorry' matching and response length. Section 3.4 adds approximately 30 hours of training on eight A800 GPUs and data-generation timings. The abstract explicitly identifies code, datasets, and models at the existing resource link; most implementation settings were already documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dong et al. (2023) on adversarial image attacks, Huang et al. (2025) on jailbreak strategy expansion, and Zhang et al. (2025) on self-memory alignment. Research positioning remains largely unchanged; most other reference edits update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused analysis paragraphs, expands the self-rewarding documentation, and makes localized abstract and grammar edits. Affiliations, correspondence, publication information, and acknowledgements are updated. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables and a boxed rating-prompt display. The original open-source and proprietary comparison tables move and become Tables 6 and 7 instead of 3 and 4. Figures 1–8 and existing table designs are retained, with accompanying page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added design analyses, cost measurements, and exact rating prompts improve supporting evidence and reproducibility. These gains are limited by unexplained AlpacaEval discrepancies: DPO-3 scores 38.66% in retained Table 1 but 35.96% in new Table 4. Claims about variance and PRM necessity also exceed the reported uncertainty evidence. Overall, v2 offers a useful but bounded improvement while retaining the original main results and theory.
